_comment: QY100 FX send-level parameters, discovered and verified 2026-08-11/12. Same XG Parameter Change message family as effect_types.json (F0 43 1n 4C aa bb cc dd F7); see ../CLAUDE.md ('Remote control over MIDI') for the full writeup.
message_format: F0 43 1n 4C aa bb cc dd F7 -- address aa bb cc, one data byte dd (continuous 0-127).

parameters.name: Reverb Send Level
parameters.note: Captured a clean sweep of 127 messages (01..7f) turning the panel knob fully up. Sent '02 01 58 00' back over MIDI IN and the send audibly/visually dropped to 0 on the device -- confirmed bidirectional, same as effect type. Distinct from the per-channel Reverb Send seen as plain CC91 in the Undo/Redo mixer-resync burst (CLAUDE.md) -- likely this address is the system/global send, CC91 the per-channel one; not yet confirmed which is which or how they interact.

parameters.name: Chorus Send Level
parameters.note: Captured the same clean 01..7f sweep turning the chorus send knob fully up, at the address immediately after Reverb Send (58 -> 59). Not yet independently sent back and confirmed changing the device (only Reverb Send got that specific test), but the parallel structure makes it very likely to behave the same way.

tested_and_negative.hypothesis: Following the 58=Reverb, 59=Chorus sequence, guessed this would be a Variation/Effect send (the panel has no visible knob for it).
tested_and_negative.result: Sent '02 01 5a 7f' (max). No audible or visual difference observed. Either not a real parameter, or real but not routed anywhere perceptible on this pattern/setup. The simple next-address-in-sequence pattern does not hold universally -- don't assume adjacent addresses are always related parameters without verifying.
